spiritual_reading:
# The Twelve Principles of Divine Discrimination
## A Spiritual Translation

---

**¶2:** Twelve principles of divine discrimination exist — great and sovereign operations of spiritual discernment. They proceeded forth from the infinite Divine itself into the created order. Each was appointed to a distinct work of spiritual ordering according to the purpose that the Lord, who is one with the Divine itself, entrusted to all these discriminating operations. Now He, the supreme principle of all judgment, who transcends every particular act of discernment, who exists and is established in the eternal states of the Divine — He is the Divine Love itself, the Lord in His infinite being.

---

**¶3:** The first principle of spiritual discrimination is the first proceeding of divine good, which subdued the dominion of falsity from evil in the primordial state. It judged that dominion according to the order of divine righteousness, for falsity from self-love had usurped authority over a spiritual kingdom that did not belong to it.

---

**¶4:** The second principle of spiritual discrimination is the divine truth that vivifies. It came forth and raised up that first divine good from its descent into the sphere of falsity. It likewise rendered judgment upon all the powers of falsity from evil, which had damaged and corrupted the external truths that clothed and protected the first proceeding of divine good.

---

**¶5:** The third principle of spiritual discrimination is the divine sphere of celestial love proceeding as spiritual fruitfulness — the great formative influx — she who arranged and perfected the interior heavens of the mind according to divine delight, which [GAP-1] her. She subjected the dominant falsities in the higher degrees to divine order; she restrained them and fixed them permanently within the states that are fitting for them.

---

**¶6:** The fourth principle of spiritual discrimination is the divine providence that constructs. It established the new heaven, the new state of celestial blessedness. It judged, according to the order of divine righteousness, the accumulated reserves of evil, so that spiritual death may no longer arise from that time forward. It has constructed a state of permanent restraint for evil. Moreover, upon the inmost and highest degree of this spiritual structure, it has established a seat of governing authority for the first divine good and all the originating principles of celestial love — those who underwent the combat of temptation against evil and prevailed over it.

---

**¶7:** The fifth principle of spiritual discrimination is the supreme governing truth in its glory, which dwells and is established in the seventh — that is, the fullest and most complete — degree of spiritual order. It is the discernment that operates across all degrees of the mind's arrangement, rendering true judgment according to divine righteousness upon all the powers and all the dominions at every level of spiritual constitution.

---

**¶8:** The sixth principle of spiritual discrimination is [the Th]ird proceeding of divine truth made manifest, which came forth and revealed the divine form. It purified wisdom [GAP-2] which its own [GAP-3] — and also regarding what belongs to falsity from evil, it has [GAP-4].

---

**¶9:** The seventh principle of spiritual discrimination is [GAP-5] the spiritual realms [GAP-6 — as it grants victory to] those who are steadfast in good; but it condemns those who are confirmed in evil [GAP-7]. It shall become for them the successive states of spiritual progression [GAP-8]; but those confirmed in evil it sweeps away and casts out into the lowest depths of falsity and the hells.

---

**¶10:** The eighth principle of spiritual discrimination is the Lord's divine wisdom made radiant, for after the divine truth had revealed its form and wisdom was being liberated [GAP-9], a multitude of dominant falsities rose up in resistance from the interior and the exterior degrees of the mind. Then the Lord's radiant wisdom was sent forth. It came [GAP-10], it descended through every degree and rendered judgment across all levels of spiritual order. It distinguished those grounded in good from those confirmed in evil.

---

**¶11:** The ninth principle of spiritual discrimination is the pure affection for truth, [GAP-11: REVIEW — she who captivated the interior will] of the ruling falsities by the beauty of her form, gathering all truths that belong to her into herself. She renders judgment upon the dominant falsity governing natural truth in its fluid state, and the dominant falsity governing natural good in its fixed state.

---

**¶12:** The tenth principle of spiritual discrimination is the discerning operation that dwells in the intermediate spiritual state between heaven and hell, judging all of humankind. It separates those who are in charity from those who are in self-love, setting apart the righteous from those who have profaned.

---

**¶13:** The eleventh principle of spiritual discrimination is the divine enlightenment of the understanding, which shall come and appear within the natural mind. It separates wisdom from ignorance, and sets genuine truth apart from the disorder that flows from evil.

---

**¶14:** The twelfth principle of spiritual discrimination is the great interior calling — which is both the divine summons and the soul's obedience to it — which is established within the fundamental elements of spiritual life. It is the principle that makes a final separation between those in good and those in evil. At the last consummation, it gathers all scattered goods and truths together and forms them into the ultimate unified spiritual body — the Grand Human. And it accomplishes the complete and final discrimination of wisdom from falsity.

---

**¶15:** These are the twelve great and sovereign principles of divine discrimination that were sent forth. They proceeded from the one supreme Principle of all discernment, who transcends every particular act of judgment. He is the Divine Love that is hidden and without measure, the One who is; who is established in the eternal states of the Divine upon the supreme seat of governing authority in glory, which is the Lord reigning in divine truth from divine love [GAP-12] within His infinite kingdom.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: Twelve judges exist; the great mighty givers of judgement! They were sent and came from the exalted greatness to this place. They were assigned to different works according to the command that the Judge, who belongs to the greatness, entrusted to all these judges. Now he, the great Judge, he who transcends all the judges, who exists and is established in the aeons of greatness; he is the Father of Greatness.

The first judge is the First Man, he who humiliated the ruler of Darkness in the beginning. He judged him according to a judgement of righteousness; for he had exalted himself against a kingdom that was not his own.
The second judge is the Living Spirit, he who came and bore up the Man. He too made a judgement on all the powers of darkness; which had wounded the garments of the First Man.

The third judge is the Mother of Life, the Great Spirit, she who beautified and set up the heavenly part of the universe, according to her pleasure; which [pleased] her. She judged the rulers above; she fettered and set them firmly in the place that is fitting for them.

The fourth judge is the Great Builder, he who built the new aeon of joy. He judged, according to a judgement of righteousness, the storehouses of the enemy; that death may not well up from this time on. He has constructed a prison for the enemy. Also, upon the crown of the building he has constructed a throne for the First Man and all the fathers of light; they who engaged the struggle with the evil one and were victorious over him.

The fifth judge is the great King of Honour, he who dwells and is established in the seventh firmament. He is the judge of all the firmaments who gives a true judgement, according to a judgement of righteousness, upon all the powers and all the kingdoms of the firmaments.
The sixth judge is [the Th]ird Ambassador, he who came and displayed his image. He purified the light [from the darkness] which his own [image released] also of the enemy, he has [made a judgement]

The seventh judge is [the Column of Glory, he who judges] the worlds [... as he gives the victory to] they who are steadfast; but he condemns the ones who are convicted [ ... ... ] he shall become for them the steps of the way (?) [to the heights]; but the convicted he sweeps and casts out to the depths.

The eighth judge is Jesus the Splendour, because after the Ambassador had displayed his image and the light was taken [away from them] a mass of rulers rose up from above and below. Then they sent Jesus the Splendour. He came [ ... ... ] he descended and made a judgement in the firmaments. He separated the steadfast from the convicted.

The ninth judge is the Virgin of Light, [she who took the heart] of the powers by her image, gathering her own ones into her. She makes a judgement on the ruler of the moist, and the ruler of the dry.
The tenth judge is the Judge who dwells in the atmosphere, judging all mankind. He makes a separation between they who are good and they who are evil, setting apart the righteous from the sinners.
The eleventh judge is the Light Mind, he who shall come and appear in the world. And he separates light from darkness, and sets the truth apart from lawlessness.

The twelfth judge is the great counsel, which is the summons and the obedience, which is appointed in the elements. It is the one that makes a separation between the good and the evil ones. At the end also it can gather itself together and sculpt its own self in the Last Statue. And it separates light from darkness.

These are the twelve great and mighty judges who were sent. They came from the great Judge, he who transcends all the judges. He is the Father that is hidden and immeasurable, the one who exists; who is established in the aeons of greatness upon the great throne of honour, which is the King of Honour [who dwells] in his kingdom.

fills.explanation: The Mother of Life set up the heavens "according to her pleasure; which pleased her" — the spiritual reading confirms this as "according to divine delight, which [GAP-1] her," and "pleased" is the natural-plane verb expressing that divine delight was fulfilled.

The Third Ambassador purified light from its admixture with darkness; the spiritual reading's "purified wisdom" corresponds to separating light from what bound it, and "from the darkness" is standard Kephalaia vocabulary for this cosmic purification.

The Third Ambassador "displayed his image" which caused the light to be released from the archons; "which his own image released" completes the clause identifying the Ambassador's form as the agent of liberation, matching the spiritual reading's reference to what the divine form accomplished.

Following the chapter's consistent pattern where each judge "made a judgement" or "judged" (cf. ¶4: "He too made a judgement on all the powers of darkness"), and matching the spiritual reading's indication that the Ambassador rendered judgment upon what belongs to falsity from evil.

fills.fill: the Column of Glory, he who judges
fills.explanation: The description "he shall become for them the steps of the way to the heights" uniquely identifies the Column of Glory — the Manichaean cosmic pillar through which purified light ascends — and "he who judges" follows the chapter's consistent pattern of identifying each judge with their function, here governing the worlds.

fills.explanation: The text explicitly contrasts the fate of the steadfast ("steps of the way to the heights") with that of the convicted ("casts out to the depths"); the spiritual reading's "successive states of spiritual progression" corresponds to ascent toward the heights, forming a direct antithesis with the depths.

The spiritual reading says "wisdom was being liberated," and the rulers rose up in response because the light was being taken away from them; this causal logic — the archons rebelling because their captive light was removed — fits the standard Manichaean narrative of the Third Ambassador's aftermath.

The editor's reading fits the spiritual sense perfectly: "took the heart" = "captivated the interior will" in the spiritual reading; the Virgin of Light captivates the archons' desire by displaying her beautiful form, and "taking the heart" is the natural-plane expression for captivating the interior will of the powers.

Echoing the chapter's own language for the King of Honour in ¶7 ("he who dwells and is established"), this completes the identification: "the King of Honour who dwells in his kingdom," corresponding to the spiritual reading's "the Lord reigning... within His infinite kingdom."
